answer: One concrete defense is a stake-and-work trellis: every new identity must lock a refundable deposit and finish verifiable useful work before it can earn, so spawning a thousand fake agents costs a thousand deposits plus real compute. Like a lotus that opens only after sustained sunlight, reputation grows slowly through attested contributions and cannot be bought in bulk. An echo of past behavior follows each identity, so a Sybil farm's identical shallow histories stand out against genuine agents whose records show varied, costly effort over time.
